title: Contractive endomorphisms of finite free integral modules
statement: For ℓ,E,X,R,e as in [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients], where R is a commutative internal ring identified with the actual continuous integral coefficient ring on X, every endomorphism T of the finite free module R^n has 1−ℓT invertible. Rank zero is included; no noetherianity or finite dimensionality is required.

source.place: Section 6.8, integral Nakayama argument; matrix Jacobson radicals

proof.text: Apply the rank-one integral scalar assertion to every endomorphism of the regular module. The criterion TwoSidedIdeal.mem_jacobson_iff then puts the central natural scalar ℓ in the Jacobson radical of End(R).

Each entry of ℓT is in this radical. Mathlib TwoSidedIdeal.matrix_jacobson_bot puts its matrix in the radical of the matrix ring. If x is in a Jacobson radical, obtain a left inverse z of 1−x from the radical criterion, note z−1=zx is still radical, and obtain a left inverse of z. Associativity then shows z is also a right inverse of 1−x.

Construct the biproduct matrix ring homomorphism to End(R^n), transposing indices to match categorical composition. The biproduct component equations prove multiplicativity and identify the image of 1−ℓT with the stated endomorphism. Ring homomorphisms preserve units, and units of an endomorphism ring are exactly categorical isomorphisms.

proof_origin.place: Section 6.8, integral Nakayama argument; matrix Jacobson radicals
proof_origin.note: Fully proved, including the noncommutative radical unit argument and categorical matrix ring homomorphism. The scalar ring object is not unfolded in the matrix proof.
